learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how to craft a compelling narrative by mastering the essential elements of character, plot, setting, and conflict in a compact format!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A story is only as good as its characters. A protagonist needs a clear motivation (what they want) and a flaw. In a short story, keep the cast small—usually just 1 to 3 important characters.
The setting is the time and place of the story. It shouldn't just be a backdrop; it should affect the mood and the characters' actions. Use sensory details to make the world feel lived-in.

main_concepts.concept_title: ⚔️ The Heart of the Story: Conflict
main_concepts.simple_explanation: No conflict = no story! The protagonist must face an obstacle. This can be internal (man vs. self) or external (man vs. man, nature, or society).
Stories follow a structure: Exposition (intro), Rising Action (things get complicated), Climax (the point of maximum tension/the big showdown), Falling Action, and Resolution (the aftermath).

Who is telling the story? First-person ('I' did this) builds intimacy. Third-person limited ('He/She' did this) focuses on one character's thoughts, while Third-person omniscient knows everyone's thoughts.

fun_activity.title: 🚪 The Closed Door Prompt
fun_activity.instructions: Write a 100-word micro-story starting with this exact sentence: 'She stared at the closed door, knowing she only had ten seconds to decide whether to open it.' Focus entirely on building suspense!

exam_tips: 📌 Start your story 'in media res' (in the middle of the action). Don't waste paragraphs on boring introductions like waking up and brushing teeth.
📌 'Show, Don't Tell' is the golden rule. Don't write 'John was sad.' Write 'John stared at the floor, his shoulders heavy as he dragged his feet.'
📌 In a short story exam, aim for a single, impactful climax rather than a complex, sprawling plot.
quick_recap: ⭐ A short story should focus on a single central incident or single period of time.
⭐ Every scene must do one of two things: advance the plot or reveal character.
⭐ The best endings are inevitable yet surprising, tying up the core conflict satisfyingly.
